current.text: Tyrese Haliburton is back. Indiana's projected starting five has Nembhard in the backcourt next to Haliburton.
From January 1 to the end of last season he was top five in assists per game.
With Haliburton back, the experts expect a lower-usage role and fewer assists. They see little upside or blow-up potential unless Haliburton is out.
Josh found him slightly underwhelming as the lead point guard.
He is the expert's biggest fade on the Pacers at Yahoo's rank of 108. ESPN's rank of 149 is called reasonable. Tier 8 among point guards.
Do not draft him in standard formats. Take him only in the late rounds or in deeper leagues. The experts prefer an upside flier over him at around pick 112.
With a March 28 season end, Indiana plays 3, 4 and 3 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21, which is not ideal. The team has 15 back-to-backs.

durable.text: He is a low-usage player with weak defensive stats and shooting percentages that go up and down.
His assist value depends on Haliburton being out.
He shoots threes badly in the regular season but has shot about 40% from three in the playoffs.

note: He went for 10 USD in our league last season. This year Yahoo values him at 4 USD (1.0 average cost, rank 108) and ESPN at 0 USD (rank 149), and the experts side with ESPN. With 144 players drafted, he is at most a 1 USD bench pick: a Haliburton handcuff whose only plus is assists (6.0 projected, his one category clearly above the pool), with nothing else to help a build. Early in the season, check his usage and assists next to a healthy Haliburton and whether Carlisle limits Haliburton's minutes. If Haliburton misses time, pick him up from waivers.
